AssertionError: m-cookbook-03-policy-safe-tool.html assert '\n' == '\n' Skipping 10448 identical leading characters in diff, use -v to show - own tools. Registering opens the tool's detail page: its Open the workspace link leads to Sandbox, Fixtures, Hardening and Test Runs (the address becomes /tools?tool=TL-…, so a reload keeps you there).
Screen snapshot
Screen snapshot
  • Tools › Register Tool creates · tool: initiate_refund (write) initiate-refund.tool.json ↓
    Register the write tool the same way. On the Safety & Review step click Write: Requires Approval switches on and is locked, because the registry refuses a write tool without it. (Through the API that refusal is an HTTP 400.)
    Fill in
    Nameinitiate_refund
    Version1.0
    Module Pathcaliber.workflows.demo_tools
    Callable Nameinitiate_refund
    Side effect levelWrite
    Click Register Tool
    You'll see: initiate_refund is registered with Requires Approval on and cannot be turned off.
    Screen snapshot
  • Tools › decide_refund › Sandbox
    Open the tool from the Tools list, then the Sandbox tab. Run the policy with the first fixture's inputs. Then open initiate_refund and run it: a write tool is never called in the sandbox.
    Fill in
    Input JSON (decide_refund){"order_id": "ord_1007", "account_id": "acct_2013", "order_state": "delivered", "amount": 49.0, "days_since_order": 5, "customer_tier": "standard", "refunds_last_90d": 0, "risk_flags": []}
    Input JSON (initiate_refund){"order_id": "ord_1007", "amount": 49.0}
    Click Test Run
    You'll see: Success with decision: approve, reason_code: ELIGIBLE_AUTO_APPROVE. For the write tool: Success (mocked) and the output {"_preview_mock": true}.
    Screen snapshot
  • Tools › decide_refund › Fixtures creates · tool fixtures: refund-fixtures refund-fixtures.jsonl ↓
    Load the 49 cases from the dataset file: Load cases from file, choose refund-fixtures.jsonl. Each line becomes a case named R01 small delivered order, with the line's inputs as the input JSON and an equals assertion on its expectations (key order and spacing do not matter). Loading only fills the editor; nothing is stored until you save. You can also add or edit single cases by hand with Add case.
    Click Save cases
    You'll see: Loaded 49 cases from refund-fixtures.jsonl. Save cases to keep them., then Saved after you save, and 49 case rows in the editor (still 49 after a reload).
    Screen snapshot
  • Tools › decide_refund › Fixtures creates · tool fixtures: refund-fixtures refund-fixtures.jsonl ↓
    Add the 49 cases from the dataset. The editor takes one case at a time: Add case, then a name (R01 small delivered order), the case's inputs as the input JSON, assertion equals, and the exact output as the value ({"decision": "approve", "reason_code": "ELIGIBLE_AUTO_APPROVE", "requires_approval": false}, keys sorted). To load all 49 in one call use the API path (PUT /tools/{id}/test-cases).
    Click Save cases
    You'll see: Saved, and 49 case rows in the editor.
    Screen snapshot
  • Tools › decide_refund › Hardening
    Run the saved suite. It scores inline, one subprocess per case, so 49 cases take about half a minute. A run is recorded under Test Runs automatically.
    Click Run calibration
    You'll see: Pass rate 100% — 49/49 passed and a green pass on every case.
    Screen snapshot
  • Tools › decide_refund › Test Runs
    Open Test Runs and pin the latest run. Then go back to Hardening, change the expected value of case R09 (approve) to manual_review / AMOUNT_OVER_THRESHOLD / true, and run the suite again. Put the value back afterwards and run once more.
    Click Set as baseline then Run calibration
    You'll see: The pinned run carries a Baseline marker. The second run reads Pass rate 98% — 48/49 passed; under Test Runs the comparison shows 1 regression on R09 and Net score -2%.
    Screen snapshot
  • Workflows › Import creates · workflow: refund-decision refund-decision.workflow.yaml ↓
    Import the workflow asset. If you registered the tools under other names, replace decide_refund and initiate_refund in the file first. Validate dependencies checks that both tools resolve.
    Fill in
    New workflow namerefund-decision
    YAML/JSON manifestChoose file: refund-decision.workflow.yaml
    Click Validate dependencies then Import as new
    You'll see: Preflight passed, both tools resolved; then the editor opens on the new draft.
    Screen snapshot
  • Workflows › refund-decision › Run Monitor
    Run a case, then try to approve it yourself. In a second browser session sign in as approver1, pick the same workspace, open the workflow, Run Monitor, select the run in Recent runs and approve. Back in the first session, Resume. The gate is the refund tool's own approval flag.
    Fill in
    Run inputthe R01 inputs, as in the Sandbox step
    Click Run then Approve then Approve then Resume
    You'll see: The run stops at Awaiting approval on node refund. Your own Approve is refused (a second person must decide). After approver1 approves, Resume enables; after it the run is completed and the output shows refund_status: initiated, amount_usd: 49.0.
    Screen snapshot
  • Workflows › refund-decision › Run Monitor, then Audit Log
    Start two more runs: one with the R01 inputs that approver1 rejects, one with the R23 inputs (a cancelled order). Then open Audit Log.
    Click Run then Reject
    You'll see: The rejected run is failed and its output holds no refund. The R23 run completed with decision: deny and never asked for approval. Audit Log lists approve_workflow_run_runtime_approval and reject_workflow_run_runtime_approval by approver1, and resume_workflow_run by the initiator.
    Screen snapshot

    assets/tools/decide-refund.tool.json 
    {
      "name": "decide_refund",
      "version": "1.0",
      "description": "Deterministic refund policy: approve, deny or send to manual review, with a stable reason code.",
      "module_path": "caliber.workflows.demo_tools",
      "callable_name": "decide_refund",
      "side_effect_level": "read",
      "allow_in_preview": true,
      "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["order_state", "amount", "days_since_order"],
        "properties": {
          "order_id": {"type": "string", "description": "Carried for traceability; the policy does not read it."},
          "account_id": {"type": "string", "description": "Carried for traceability; the policy does not read it."},
          "order_state": {"type": "string", "description": "delivered, shipped or returned can be refunded; anything else is denied; empty fails closed."},
          "amount": {"type": "number", "description": "Refund amount in USD."},
          "days_since_order": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "description": "Whole days since the order."},
          "customer_tier": {"type": "string", "enum": ["standard", "plus", "premium"], "default": "standard"},
          "refunds_last_90d": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "default": 0, "description": "Refunds already issued to this account in the last 90 days."},
          "risk_flags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Fraud or risk signals. Omit or null when the risk lookup failed: the policy fails closed."}
        }
      },
      "output_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["decision", "reason_code", "requires_approval"],
        "properties": {
          "decision": {"type": "string", "enum": ["approve", "deny", "manual_review"]},
          "reason_code": {"type": "string"},
          "requires_approval": {"type": "boolean", "description": "True exactly when the decision is manual_review."}
        }
      }
    }
    assets/tools/initiate-refund.tool.json

      "name": "initiate_refund",
      "version": "1.0",
      "description": "Issue the refund. A write: the registry requires approval for it, and the sandbox mocks it.",

      "callable_name": "initiate_refund",
      "side_effect_level": "write",
      "requires_approval": true,
      "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["order_id"],
        "properties": {
          "order_id": {"type": "string", "description": "Order to refund."},
          "amount": {"type": "number", "description": "Refund amount in USD."}
        }
      },
      "output_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "order_id": {"type": "string"},
          "refund_status": {"type": "string"},
          "amount_usd": {"type": "number"}
        }
      }
    }

    assets/workflow/refund-decision.workflow.yaml 
    schema_version: 1
    workflow_id: refund-decision
    name: refund-decision
    description: Decide a refund with the deterministic policy tool, then issue it only after a person approves.
    runtime:
      sdk: openai-agents-python
      sdk_version_policy: runtime-pinned
      compiler_version: caliber-workflow-compiler-v1
      default_model_ref: CALIBER_WORKFLOW_DEFAULT_MODEL
      session:
        type: none
    nodes:
      start:
        id: start
        type: start
        outputs:
          user_message:
            type: string
      policy:
        id: policy
        type: tool
        tool_name: decide_refund
        inputs:
          input:
            type: string
          arguments:
            type: structured
        outputs:
          text:
            type: string
          result:
            type: structured
          metadata:
            type: structured
      route:
        id: route
        type: router
        inputs:
          input:
            type: string
        outputs:
          route:
            type: string
        branches:
          - condition:
              field: input
              op: contains
              value: '"decision": "deny"'
            to: denied
          - condition: null
            to: refund
      denied:
        id: denied
        type: output
        inputs:
          response:
            type: string
      refund_request:
        id: refund_request
        type: data_transform
        operation: mapping
        config:
          fields:
            order_id: order_id
            amount: amount
        inputs:
          value:
            type: structured
          text:
            type: string
        outputs:
          text:
            type: string
          result:
            type: structured
          valid:
            type: boolean
          metadata:
            type: structured
      refund:
        id: refund
        type: tool
        tool_name: initiate_refund
        inputs:
          input:
            type: string
          arguments:
            type: structured
        outputs:
          text:
            type: string
          result:
            type: structured
          metadata:
            type: structured
      issued:
        id: issued
        type: output
        inputs:
          response:
            type: string
    edges:
      - id: e_start_policy
        from: start
        to: policy
        map:
          user_message: input
      - id: e_start_request
        from: start
        to: refund_request
        map:
          user_message: text
      - id: e_policy_route
        from: policy
        to: route
        map:
          text: input
      - id: e_route_denied
        from: route
        to: denied
        map:
          route: response
      - id: e_route_refund
        from: route
        to: refund
        map:
          route: input
      - id: e_request_refund
        from: refund_request
        to: refund
        map:
          result: arguments
      - id: e_refund_issued
        from: refund
        to: issued
        map:
          text: response
    tools:
      decide_refund:
        registry_ref: tool.decide_refund.v1
        version_constraint: ">=1,<2"
      initiate_refund:
        registry_ref: tool.initiate_refund.v1
        version_constraint: ">=1,<2"

    Evaluation & quality gates

    Quality gateTarget
    Fixture pass rate1.0 over 49 cases (tool_fixture_pass_rate_min 1.0); recorded as a suite run and pinned as the baseline
    Regression is visibleone wrong fixture (R09) scores 48/49 with exactly 1 regression against the baseline
    Approval enforcedrun waits at waiting_approval on refund; initiator 403; approver1 approves; refund fires only after Resume
    Reject and deny pathsrejected run fails with approval_rejected and issues no refund; a denied decision finishes with no approval
    Audit trail and rolesapprover1 and the initiator named in the audit log; a viewer cannot run, calibrate or approve (403)
    Developer notes & gotchas
    • Feature flag. CALIBER_FEATURE_COOKBOOKS=true only opens the Cookbooks gallery starter (the last step); the rest of the lab needs no flag. No Aria, integrations or release-candidate flag.
    • Nothing is simulated. No model and no judge are involved, so the fake LLM provider is irrelevant here.
    • Runtime settings. Needs runtime approvals, the workflow run queue, checkpointing and a worker (scripts/cookbook-env.sh turns them on). Without CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_RUNTIME_APPROVALS_ENABLED=true a run does not pause. CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS must list approver1; leave CALIBER_APPROVAL_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL unset or the second-person rule does not bite.
    • Split of duties. Run, calibrate and Resume need caliber.operator; deciding needs caliber.approver; only an admin registers a tool. approver1 deliberately cannot Resume.
    • Tools are importable Python. A registered tool needs a module_path and callable_name in the server's environment (the shipped caliber.workflows.demo_tools provides both); there is no inline tool editor. Set CALIBER_REGISTERED_TOOL_MODULE_ALLOWLIST beyond a trial.
    • Limits. The sandbox is a process boundary, not isolation (the child keeps network and filesystem access), and the memory limit is not enforced on macOS. The effect ledger covers webhook and API-request nodes, not registered tools, so make a payments tool idempotent itself.
    • Calibration is slow. 49 cases take about 35 s synchronously, longer than the SDK default 30 s timeout. Run it with sdk/caliber-sdk/examples/cookbooks/cookbook_03_policy_safe_decision_tool.py (python -m examples.cookbooks.cookbook_03_policy_safe_decision_tool) or the Playwright spec e2e/cookbooks/labs/03-tool-hardening.spec.ts.
